questions.stem: A man buys an article for Rs. 300 and sells it for Rs. 360. What is his exact profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Cost Price (CP) = 300. Selling Price (SP) = 360. Profit = 360 - 300 = 60. Profit % = (Profit / CP) * 100 = (60 / 300) * 100 = 20%.

questions.stem: If the cost price is 80% of the selling price, what is the profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Let SP = 100. Then CP = 80. Profit = 100 - 80 = 20. Profit % = (Profit / CP) * 100 = (20 / 80) * 100 = 25%.

questions.stem: The cost price of 20 articles is the same as the selling price of x articles. If the profit is 25%, find the precise value of x.
questions.explanation: Let CP of 1 article = Rs. 1. CP of x articles = x. SP of x articles = CP of 20 articles = 20. Profit = 20 - x. Profit % = ((20 - x) / x) * 100 = 25. So, (20 - x) / x = 1/4 => 80 - 4x = x => 5x = 80 => x = 16.

questions.stem: A man sold two chairs for Rs. 1200 each. On one he gained 20% and on the other he lost 20%. What is his net loss or gain percentage in the entire transaction?
questions.explanation: When two identical items are sold at the same price, one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%, there is always a net loss. The loss percentage is calculated as (x^2) / 100. Here x = 20. Loss % = (20^2) / 100 = 400 / 100 = 4% loss.

questions.stem: A dishonest dealer professes to sell his goods at cost price, but he uses a weight of 900 grams for the kg weight. Find his exact gain percentage.
questions.explanation: He sells 900g of goods but charges the customer for 1000g (1 kg). His profit is the 100g he didn't give. Profit % = (Error / True Weight) * 100 = (100 / 900) * 100 = 100 / 9 % = 11.11%.
